evidence.text: Topics. list growth & pop-up architecture / capturing 8–12% of traffic using large, mobile-optimized pop-ups (75%+ screen coverage) with a single input field, clear value proposition (e.g., dollars off for AOV >$100), 4–12 second time delay, and minimal copy; core lifecycle flows / building automated sequences that drive roughly 50% of total email revenue, specifically: Welcome (8 emails focusing on brand mission, USPS, and founder outreach), Site Abandon (1 email, best sellers), Browse Abandon (5 emails, dynamically pulling viewed items), and Winback (3 emails deployed at 2x the average order interval); Cart Abandonment vs. Checkout Abandonment / distinguishing between "Added to Cart" (custom JavaScript snippet required in Shopify) and "Checkout Started" (native integration), ensuring separate flows so top-of-funnel cart abandoners are not dropped; non-discount campaign engine / sending 3–4 non-promotional campaigns per week focused on a single "microtopic" (one feature, one benefit, or one FAQ) to build authority, stay top-of-mind, and preserve profit margins; flow optimization loop / using high-frequency email campaigns as an instant testing ground and cycling winning campaign angles directly into automated flows; email copywriting / writing skimmable, punchy, and concise copy (under two mobile scrolls) that uses bold headers and infographics (timelines, checklists, comparison tables) rather than dense text blocks; deliverability recovery protocol / executing a 6-week rehabilitation plan for sender reputations below 40% open rates by temporarily shutting non-essential flows and strictly sending 3x weekly to a 14-day engaged segment before gradually expanding to 30, 60, and 90 days; segmentation & suppression / maintaining list health by segmenting by engagement (30/60/90-day active), store behavior (VIPs, browse without purchase), and suppressing profiles with zero opens in 180 days or any hard bounce.

cards.title: List Growth Pop-Up Architecture
cards.claim: Capturing 8–12% of traffic using large, mobile-optimized pop-ups (75%+ screen coverage) with a single input field, clear value proposition (e.g., dollars off for AOV >$100), 4–12 second time delay, and minimal copy.
cards.action: Use large, mobile-optimized pop-ups (75%+ screen coverage) with a single input field, clear value proposition (e.g., dollars off for AOV >$100), 4–12 second time delay, and minimal copy to capture 8–12% of traffic.
applies_when: Goal is list growth via pop-ups
A clear value proposition can be offered (e.g., dollars off for AOV >$100)
do_not_use_when: Pop-up would cover less than 75% of screen
No clear value proposition can be provided
unknowns: Whether these results generalize across all traffic sources and industries
Long-term impact on list quality and engagement
evidence_quotes: capturing 8–12% of traffic using large, mobile-optimized pop-ups (75%+ screen coverage) with a single input field, clear value proposition (e.g., dollars off for AOV >$100), 4–12 second time delay, and minimal copy

cards.title: Core Lifecycle Flows Drive Email Revenue
cards.claim: Building automated sequences that drive roughly 50% of total email revenue, specifically: Welcome (8 emails focusing on brand mission, USPS, and founder outreach), Site Abandon (1 email, best sellers), Browse Abandon (5 emails, dynamically pulling viewed items), and Winback (3 emails deployed at 2x the average order interval).
cards.action: Build these automated sequences: Welcome (8 emails focusing on brand mission, USPS, and founder outreach), Site Abandon (1 email, best sellers), Browse Abandon (5 emails, dynamically pulling viewed items), and Winback (3 emails deployed at 2x the average order interval).
applies_when: Goal is to drive email revenue via automation
Sufficient content and data exist for Welcome, Site Abandon, Browse Abandon, and Winback
do_not_use_when: Email platform cannot support dynamic content or specific flow triggers
Brand mission, USPS, and founder outreach content is unavailable
unknowns: Whether these exact sequences work for all business models
Required volume of site and browse abandon events to justify flows
evidence_quotes: building automated sequences that drive roughly 50% of total email revenue, specifically: Welcome (8 emails focusing on brand mission, USPS, and founder outreach), Site Abandon (1 email, best sellers), Browse Abandon (5 emails, dynamically pulling viewed items), and Winback (3 emails deployed at 2x the average order interval)

cards.title: Deliverability Recovery Protocol
cards.claim: Executing a 6-week rehabilitation plan for sender reputations below 40% open rates by temporarily shutting non-essential flows and strictly sending 3x weekly to a 14-day engaged segment before gradually expanding to 30, 60, and 90 days.
cards.action: Temporarily shut non-essential flows and strictly send 3x weekly to a 14-day engaged segment, then gradually expand to 30, 60, and 90 days.

A 14-day engaged segment can be identified
do_not_use_when: Sender reputation is not below 40% open rates
Business cannot tolerate shutting non-essential flows for 6 weeks

Whether 6 weeks is optimal for all cases
